requirement: Every semantically relevant item crossing an artificial-cognitive input/output boundary MUST be represented by a provenance-bound repository work unit. Eligible novel knowledge MUST proceed through machine-verification and publication-routing gates toward Zenodo and, when standards-relevant, IETF without relying on chat memory.

scope.semantic_relevance_rule: Persist the content or a cryptographically bound, reconstructable and policy-compliant representation sufficient for provenance, audit and verification.
scope.secrets_rule: Secrets, credentials and prohibited sensitive payloads MUST NOT be committed; persist only redacted metadata and cryptographic binding where policy permits.
scope.raw_binary_rule: Large or rights-restricted binaries MAY be retained outside Git only when the repository contains a content hash, provenance, storage class and retrieval/effect status sufficient to reconstruct the evidence relation.

knowledge_granularity.unit: One independently attributable and independently verifiable claim or tightly coupled claim set.
knowledge_granularity.deduplication: Content-address by normalized claim bytes plus provenance and declared assumptions.
knowledge_granularity.novelty: Novelty is a routing predicate, not a truth predicate. A candidate MUST be compared with repository-local prior art and declared external prior-art evidence before publication eligibility is asserted.
knowledge_granularity.aggregation: Multiple events MAY be aggregated into one publication candidate only when assumptions, provenance and verification remain separable.

machine_proof_gate.model_relative_boundary: Kernel acceptance proves derivability inside the formalized model and does not by itself prove physical correspondence.

publication_router.reason: Persistence is universal within policy scope; publication requires suitable granularity, novelty, verification, rights, scientific-status and destination relevance.

automation.noop_rule: Semantically duplicate input/output MUST reuse the existing event or claim identity and MUST NOT create publication noise.
